claims.text: The initial alloy is an equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr random solid solution.
The random HfNbTaTiZr state has high lattice distortion caused by atomic-size mismatch and random chemical distribution.
Intrinsic disorder strongly scatters phonons and suppresses lattice thermal conductivity in the random-solid-solution baseline.
Monte Carlo annealing can induce chemical short-range order in multi-principal-element or refractory high-entropy alloys.
Annealing at 800–1200 K induces the proposed short-range order in HfNbTaTiZr.
The induced short-range order specifically produces HfTi and TiZr binary clusters.
The HfTi and TiZr clusters undergo a percolative transition to B2-like ordered structures.
B2-like ordering reduces local lattice-distortion amplitudes relative to the random solid solution.
Short-range order reduces the variance of local atomic environments and thereby reduces lattice distortion.
The ordered B2-like regions have softer force constants and reduced mass and force-constant fluctuations for selected phonon modes.
Percolation of the ordered clusters creates continuous low-scattering pathways for phonon transport.
The ordered percolating network reduces high-frequency phonon-DOS broadening and increases phonon lifetimes and mean free paths, particularly for high-frequency acoustic modes.
Percolative B2-like ordering increases lattice thermal conductivity by 15–30% relative to the random solid solution.
The conductivity increase is accompanied by sharper high-frequency phonon-DOS peaks and smaller atomic displacement amplitudes or Debye–Waller factors in ordered regions.
Below the cluster-percolation threshold, isolated ordered clusters act as scattering centers and decrease lattice thermal conductivity.
At ordering levels above the beneficial percolation regime, large precipitates can form and reintroduce strong phonon scattering.
At sufficiently high temperature, anharmonic phonon scattering can dominate and obscure the conductivity benefit of ordering.
Competing phases such as sigma phase could alter the phonon spectrum and transport behavior.
